objective: Make the Windows cmd.exe launch of a bun.cmd shim (and of pi) safe for paths with spaces, and update the remaining wrapper text in docs/pi/orchestration.md.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-win, branch release/0.3.0/fix/pi-windows-launch, head 2cfd3be (committed; your edits are a new change on top).

A bun.cmd shim found under a folder with a space (for example C:\Users\Jane Doe\AppData\Roaming\npm\bun.cmd) is started as cmd.exe /d /c "<path>" ...; with /c, when the line starts with a quote and holds more than two, cmd strips the first and last quote and the command breaks. Build the cmd.exe command line so a quoted program path and quoted arguments survive (the usual form is /d /s /c followed by the whole command line in one extra pair of quotes), apply it to every cmd.exe launch the extension makes, and test the exact argv for a spaced path and spaced arguments under a stubbed win32. Keep every argument a separate, quoted token so no cmd metacharacter in a path is interpreted, and say in the report how the arguments reach cmd.exe (Pi's exec, Node spawn with windowsVerbatimArguments or not), since that decides the quoting.

docs/pi/orchestration.md lines 31 and 81 still describe the wrapper and a bare bun; describe the Bun lookup (PATH, BUN_INSTALL/bin, ~/.bun/bin, bun.exe or a bun.cmd shim on Windows) and that the extension, not the wrapper, starts the CLI.
